title: Add plan-time policy prober and post-apply VPC health-prober into Terraform CI/CD
creator: Liam Chen
description: We need a robust CI/CD enhancement that performs policy checks at plan-time and runs lightweight health probes after Terraform apply for VPC/private deployments. This ticket implements a plan-time policy prober that executes OPA/Conftest rules against plan JSON and an after-apply health-prober stage that runs non-invasive probes (subnet reachability, route table sanity, endpoint enumerations) to detect misconfigurations before we declare the deployment successful.
background: Recent Private/VPC deployments have had a few production incidents caused by subtle Terraform changes: missing route propagation, accidental public egress for internal subnets, and service endpoint misconfigurations. Existing CI runs Conftest on modules but doesn't provide a staged prober that can evaluate plan-level diffs with workload-specific policy sets, nor a lightweight health check that runs immediately post-apply to catch runtime misconfigurations that IaC linting misses. This makes rollouts riskier for customers on Private and Dedicated environments.
goals: 1) Block risky changes earlier by surfacing plan-time policy violations with contextual guidance and auto-suggested fixes. 2) Execute a standardized set of non-destructive health probes after apply to validate critical VPC invariants. 3) Integrate the prober and health checks into existing GitHub Actions / Concourse pipelines with clear failure modes and an easy opt-out for experimental modules.
success_metrics: - Reduce post-deploy VPC incidents by 60% for private deployments in the next quarter. - 90% of policy violations surfaced at plan-time (not in prod). - Average time to detect a misconfiguration reduced from 4 hours to <15 minutes for staged rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: - Plan pipeline runs a policy-prober step that consumes `terraform show -json` and returns a structured policy report in CI artifacts. - Policy failures fail the pipeline with links to the failing policy, the exact plan patch, and remediation hints. - Post-apply pipeline runs a configurable `vpc-health-prober` that implements a pre-approved checklist (subnet overlap, route table, NAT config, security group wide-open checks, private endpoint presence) and emits pass/fail + diagnostics. - Documentation page (Confluence) describing how to add module-specific policy tests. - Tests (unit + e2e in staging) covering happy path and at least 4 failure modes. - Security review completed and signed off.
implementation_plan: 1) Build a plan-prober runner (Go) that: - Ingests `terraform plan -out=tfplan; terraform show -json tfplan` - Runs OPA/Conftest policies that accept plan JSON input - Produces a SARIF-like policy artifact with rule IDs, severity, and exact JSON path hits. 2) Create a `vpc-health-prober` (Python) that: - Accepts inventory (VPC id / TF outputs) from post-apply context - Runs non-destructive checks: verify subnet CIDR ranges, route table associations, NAT Gateway vs. public subnet placement, presence/absence of IGW, endpoint DNS records for internal services - Reports as structured JSON and summary to CI logs and to a Redash dashboard. 3) Add GitHub Actions step templates: - `plan-prober` to run after `terraform plan` and before human approval - `post-apply-vpc-prober` to run as the last step of apply workflows. 4) Policy catalog: author initial OPA bundle `redwood/vpc` with ~12 rules covering data exfiltration, public ingress, missing endpoints, and sensitive resource tags. 5) Dashboarding: push prober results to the infra observability topic (Logstash -> ES) with a quick Kibana dashboard for recent failures. 6) Tests: unit tests for policy runner, integration test against a local `kind`-like mock infra and a staged apply in the sandbox AWS account. 7) Rollout: enable for all private-VPC module PRs with a 2-week monitoring window, then promote to reserved capacity module pipelines.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): 1 week - enable for infra-team-owned VPC modules only. Alert on failures to #infra-iac and create auto-issue in Linear for any unique policy hits. Phase B: 2 weeks - extend to all private-deploy PRs with optional opt-out label `ci:skip-prober`. Phase C: GA - enforce prober failures as hard pipeline failures for high-severity rules (P0/P1). Add health-prober to production apply jobs with a soft-fail to collect signals for 2 weeks before hardening.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for plan-prober with crafted plan JSON fixtures. - Conftest rule suite coverage reports. - Integration: create a sandbox VPC via Terraform in a staging account and run full pipeline; assert prober catches intentionally injected faults (overlap CIDR, public subnet tags missing). - Post-apply tests: use a mocked AWS SDK to simulate route table states and ensure health-prober diagnostics are accurate. - Load test policy-prober with 50 parallel plan artifacts to validate runtime charing and memory usage.
rollback_and_fail_modes: - If plan-prober causes excessive false positives, pipeline gate: revert to advisory mode (warnings only) by setting `PROBER_MODE=advisory`. - If health-prober causes unacceptable apply slowdowns, run in background reporter mode for 14 days (post-apply not blocking apply). - Provide a documented debug workflow to skip a single run (comment-based opt-out on PR with `infra/iac:force-apply`) subject to audit. - In all skip cases an audit ticket is created for later review.
risks_and_mitigation: - False positives from policy rules: mitigate with a review board for new rules and require test cases for each rule. - Increased CI time: optimize prober to run incremental checks and cache previous plan hashes. - Secrets exposure: plan JSON may contain sensitive data; prober will redact secrets and operate in ephemeral runner containers with minimal retention. - Operational burden: provide curated rulesets per team and enable per-repo configuration to avoid global noise.
open_questions: - Should high-severity network exposure rules auto-block applies or only block merges? - Where should we store the OPA bundle artifact for versioning (Git vs. S3)? - Do we want to integrate a UI in Redwood Console to show prober results per-deployment?
updates: 2025-03-02: Spike completed - built a PoC plan-prober that runs Conftest against a Terraform plan JSON. PoC repo: github.com/redwood/infrastructure/plan-prober-poc (private).
2025-03-04: Security reviewed PoC; requirement added to redact sensitive fields from plan JSON. Raised VOICE-SEC-12 in security tracker.

2025-03-06: Prototype health-prober checklist implemented in python; validated subnet and route table checks against sandbox account; found and fixed an existing route propagation bug in infra-tests account.
2025-03-08: PR opened for plan-prober runner and GitHub Actions template: PR #4821. Requesting review from @infra-team and @platform-sre.
2025-03-10: Decided to gate enforcement: start with advisory mode for 7 days after rollout to all infra repos. Action: add `PROBER_MODE` env flag to workflow template.
practical_notes: - Team owners should add `prober-config.yaml` at module root to opt-in custom policies. - Default behavior: use `redwood/vpc:stable` bundle if no module-specific bundle is present. - Use `terraform validate` + plan-prober ordering: validate -> fmt/lint -> plan -> plan-prober -> human-approval -> apply -> post-apply-prober.
